title: Vaani Telugu — Spoken-First A0 to C2

baseLanguage.name: English
baseLanguage.designRule: All meanings/glosses are keyed by base-language code so another base language can be added later without changing Telugu concept IDs.

contentStatus.note: This file is designed as the stable master course contract and contains a high-confidence spoken-first seed corpus. No finite static file can itself guarantee C2; C2 requires extensive unseen listening/interaction and native-reviewed advanced corpus. The schema is intended not to require restructuring when more reviewed Telugu corpus/audio is added.

displayPolicy.script: Always store and display Telugu script.
displayPolicy.romanization: Always available on demand; shown by default for beginner material.
displayPolicy.meaning: Every first exposure must display an English meaning. Every learner-facing Telugu token/chunk must support hover/tap gloss resolution.
displayPolicy.audio: Every production-target item should support audio; human/native-reviewed audio is preferred, TTS may be fallback.
displayPolicy.unknownWordRule: A0-A2: never require a learner to understand/produce an unexplained lexical concept. B1-C2 inference tasks may contain unfamiliar language only when explicitly marked and hover/tap glosses remain available.

sessionPolicy.rule: There is no fixed daily ceiling. Each session independently receives an adaptive new-content allowance. A learner studying 3-4 hours may receive new content in later sessions if retention/review burden remains healthy.

guidance.condition: strong retention and >=90% independent recall with manageable review backlog

adaptiveNewContent.important: These are planner bands, not a proficiency score and not a daily cap.

newConceptIntroductionContract: show at least one natural context
never grade a word before its first explained exposure

sessionMix.principle: Interleave new material, same-session recall, due reviews, listening and speaking rather than blocking all new words together.
sessionMix.advancedRule: As level and review burden rise, reduce new-word proportion and increase extended listening, spontaneous speaking and transfer.

rules: Failed recall schedules earlier review and/or re-teaching in a different context.
Correct-after-hint is weaker evidence than independent recall.
Very slow correct recall is weaker evidence than fluent recall.
Fast independent delayed recall expands spacing.
Repeated contextual success is required before strong mastery.
Speaking and listening evidence are tracked separately from simple recognition.

contentRules: Prefer natural contemporary spoken Telugu over bookish/formal wording for production targets.
Keep useful formal/written alternatives as register variants rather than deleting them.
Use stable concept IDs independent of spelling.
Do not create a new concept merely because spelling/romanization was corrected.
A concept may have multiple natural accepted responses.
Do not force literal English-to-Telugu word order.
Do not use one exact canned sentence as the only valid conversational response.
Modern natural loanwords may be taught when they are genuinely common in speech.
Regional variants must be labeled; broad contemporary Telugu is the default productive target.

units.title: Sound before script
units.goal: Understand and reproduce the core sound contrasts used in common speech.

units.title: First contact
units.goal: Greet, give a name, ask a name, say yes/no, thank and apologise.

units.title: Immediate needs
units.goal: Ask for water, food, help and a bathroom.

units.title: Here and there
units.goal: Understand basic location and movement.

units.title: People around me
units.goal: Identify close family and common people.

units.title: Numbers and time basics
units.goal: Use 1-10, simple prices and now/today/tomorrow.

units.title: Daily routine
units.goal: Talk about waking, eating, going, working and sleeping.

units.title: Food and ordering
units.goal: Order common food/drink and change a simple order.

units.title: Shopping
units.goal: Ask price, quantity, choose and pay.

units.title: Travel
units.goal: Use bus/train/auto, ticket, destination and simple directions.

units.title: Home and family
units.goal: Describe home, family and possession.

units.title: Health basics
units.goal: Say pain, fever, medicine and need a doctor.

units.title: Work and study
units.goal: Say where you work/study and basic tasks.

units.title: Social basics
units.goal: Likes, invitations, simple feelings and plans.

units.title: Past events
units.goal: Explain what happened yesterday or earlier.

units.title: Plans and future
units.goal: Talk about tomorrow, weekend and future intentions.

units.title: Descriptions
units.goal: Describe people, places, objects and differences.

units.title: Requests and services
units.goal: Handle repairs, deliveries, appointments and service problems.

units.title: Longer social talk
units.goal: Sustain several turns about interests, family and experiences.

units.title: Phone and messaging
units.goal: Handle simple calls, missed calls and messages.

units.title: Reasons and choices
units.goal: Give simple reasons and preferences.

units.title: Unexpected problems
units.goal: Lost item, wrong route, delay and misunderstanding.

units.title: Connected storytelling
units.goal: Tell a coherent personal story with sequence, cause and result.

units.title: Opinions with reasons
units.goal: Explain and support an opinion on familiar topics.

units.title: Workplace conversation
units.goal: Participate in meetings, task updates and routine professional interaction.

units.title: Travel complications
units.goal: Handle cancellations, changes, complaints and alternatives.

units.title: Relationships and emotions
units.goal: Talk naturally about emotions, friendship and interpersonal problems.

units.title: Media and entertainment
units.goal: Discuss films, music, news and recommendations.

units.title: Explain how things work
units.goal: Give instructions and explain processes.

units.title: Unprepared conversation
units.goal: Maintain conversation when topic shifts unexpectedly.

units.title: Abstract discussion
units.goal: Discuss education, technology, environment and social change.

units.title: Debate without scripts
units.goal: State, defend, soften and revise a position.

units.title: Professional depth
units.goal: Present a problem, options, trade-offs and recommendation.

units.title: Native-speed everyday speech
units.goal: Follow fast connected conversational Telugu with normal repair.

units.title: Humour and implication intro
units.goal: Recognise common teasing, indirectness and implied stance.

units.title: Formal vs casual
units.goal: Switch appropriately between casual, polite and professional forms.

units.title: Long-form narrative
units.goal: Understand and produce extended stories and explanations.

units.title: Unfamiliar scenarios
units.goal: Transfer known language to situations not directly rehearsed.

units.title: Nuanced argument
units.goal: Express fine distinctions, reservations and layered reasoning.

units.title: Professional and academic speech
units.goal: Follow and contribute to specialised discussion in familiar domains.

units.title: Idiomatic conversation
units.goal: Understand and appropriately use common idiomatic/colloquial expressions.

units.title: Complex listening
units.goal: Follow long unscripted speech, interviews and discussions.

units.title: Mediation
units.goal: Explain, summarise and reformulate complex information for another person.

units.title: Style and register control
units.goal: Shift language according to relationship, purpose and setting.

units.title: Unrestricted spontaneous interaction
units.goal: Sustain precise, fluent speech across unfamiliar and demanding topics.

units.title: Fine shades of meaning
units.goal: Reformulate to express subtle distinctions and avoid ambiguity.

units.title: Implicit meaning and allusion
units.goal: Infer unstated links, humour, irony and culturally grounded allusion from context.

units.title: Complex synthesis
units.goal: Integrate and orally summarise multiple long sources and viewpoints.

units.title: Regional and colloquial comprehension
units.goal: Adapt to substantial variation in natural speech after reasonable acclimatisation.

units.title: C2 unseen performance
units.goal: Demonstrate ability on material and situations never rehearsed in the course.

meaning.en: I like it / it pleased me
it is possible / it can happen
to reformulate / say in another way

utterancePatterns.teluguPattern: ఇది పని చేయడం లేదు. రిపేర్ చేయగలరా?
utterancePatterns.romanizationPattern: idi pani cheyadam ledu. repair cheyagalaraa?

meaningPattern.en: This isn't working. Can you repair it?
I think / it seems to me that {CLAUSE}.
The main reason for that is {REASON}.

assessmentPolicy.principle: Course completion does not equal proficiency.

levels.A0-A2: Primarily guided but must include delayed recall and unseen recombination.
levels.B1-B2: Increasingly unseen listening, multi-turn speaking, narration, explanation and transfer.
levels.C1-C2: Predominantly unseen extended material, spontaneous production, register/pragmatics, inference, synthesis and reformulation.

c2ExitCapabilities: follow long natural-speed speech with minimal support
express fine distinctions and reformulate precisely
understand common idiomatic and colloquial language in context
adapt register to relationship and setting
infer unstated links, humour and implication from context
sustain extended coherent speaking without scripted prompts

readingPolicy.rule: Telugu script is always present, but script decoding must not block early speaking progress. Romanization remains available. A dedicated literacy expansion may later deepen reading/writing without changing concept IDs.

mustPass: every lexical concept has stable id, Telugu, romanization and English meaning
every production item has an explained first exposure
every A0-A2 sentence/pattern has glossable component concepts
formal variants are not silently substituted for everyday spoken production forms
SRS includes 1,2,3,5,7,14 day milestones and continues indefinitely
contentValidation.nativeReviewGate: Before declaring the corpus linguistically final, a qualified native Telugu reviewer should approve pronunciation, spoken naturalness, register, regional neutrality and all C1/C2 idiomatic/pragmatic content.
